title: Does faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi reduce to Shannon entropy? — Phi (integration) vs entropy (information) double-dissociation across an ECA substrate panel
question: Across a panel of ECA substrates, does faithful state-averaged big-Phi co-vary with Shannon output-entropy (Pearson r >= 0.5), i.e. does Phi reduce to information content?
engine: HEXAD/IIT4/lib (reused, NOT reinvented): iit4_eca.eca_tpm + iit4_bigphi.big_phi + iit4_pow2 (via stdlib/consciousness/*). Entropy + Pearson = generic stats inlined in the per-experiment harness.
runtime: $0 mac-local · hexa-only · LLM none · NO GPU · deterministic (cross-process byte-identical)

metric_defs.H_out: Shannon entropy (bits) of the OUTPUT-STATE distribution under a uniform input ensemble: o(s)=sum_i next_bit_i(s)*2^i, then H=-sum_o p(o) log2 p(o). bijection => H=4 (info-preserving); constant => H=0 (info-destroying). range [0, n].
metric_defs.Phi_mean: mean over all 2^n states of big_phi(tpm, n, st)[0] (state-averaged faithful integration).
metric_defs.correlate: Pearson r(H_out, Phi_mean) over the 10-rule panel.

seed_hypothesis_H1: REDUCTIVE (tested, may be falsified): Pearson r(H_out, Phi_mean) >= 0.5 (Phi co-varies with Shannon entropy).

max_H_zero_Phi.meaning: maximal information, zero integration — bijection preserves all bits but cells are causally independent

max_Phi_sub_max_H.meaning: most-integrated substrate is NOT the most-informative — Phi-max != H-max

double_dissociation.verdict: at fixed high entropy (H_out=4.0) Phi spans 0.0 (rule 204) to 5.625 (rule 150) — no monotone H->Phi map possible

criteria.C1_DISSOCIATION: PASS (rule 204 max-H/zero-Phi witness + rule 60 Phi=13.625 at H=3.0)

falsifiers.F287_1_DISSOCIATION_WITNESS: PASS  (204 H_out=4.0 Phi_mean=0.0; best integrating rule 60 Phi_mean=13.625 > 0.5)

checks: 11 PASS / 0 FAIL (measurement-validity gate, distinct from the H1 verdict)
finding: Faithful causal IIT 4.0 big-Phi does NOT reduce to Shannon entropy (Pearson r=0.363 < 0.5). Decisive DOUBLE dissociation: (i) identity rule 204 and complement rule 51 have MAXIMAL output entropy (4.0 bit, full bijection) yet big-Phi=0 (cells causally independent) — maximal-information zero-integration substrates; (ii) conversely the most-integrated rule 60 (Phi_mean=13.625) has SUB-MAX entropy (3.0 bit). At fixed H_out=4.0, Phi spans 0.0 to 5.625 — no monotone relation. Information (entropy) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for integration (Phi). IIT's foundational distinction holds on the LIFE lane's own substrate. Extends the 'X perp Phi' signature family (H_265/H_275/H_279) with the most fundamental X (Shannon entropy).
honest_limits: L1: n=4 small, 10-rule panel — witness existence robust, exact r value panel-dependent.
L2: output-image entropy is ONE Shannon measure (transfer/steady-state differ); 204=4bit/0=0bit endpoints definition-robust, r value definition-dependent.
L3: Phi_mean averages a state-dependent quantity (FAITHFUL_REMEASURE 4) — direction robust, magnitude hedge.
L4: ECA rules are information/integration proxies, not the things themselves; labels are substrate-themes, not phenomenal claims.
L5: structure-cut big-Phi, not full-IIT4 absolute calibration; conclusion (Phi perp H) is absence-of-correlation, robust to scale offset.
L6: closed-negative asymmetry — r=0.363>0 (weak positive residual from constant rules' (0,0)); claim is 'non-reducible', not 'fully orthogonal'.
L7: verdict is a measurement fact on a toy substrate, NOT the metaphysical claim 'consciousness is not information'.

verify_fence.claim: H_287 faithful IIT 4.0 big-Phi does NOT reduce to Shannon entropy across a 10-rule ECA panel (Pearson r=0.363 < 0.5); decisive double dissociation — identity rule 204 has MAX output-entropy (4.0 bit) yet ZERO integration, while the most-integrated rule 60 (Phi_mean=13.6) has sub-max entropy (3.0 bit); deterministic toy-substrate outcome, NOT an atlas identity
verify_fence.reason: imagination/metaphor class (hexa-bio AXIS) — verification N/A by design; values are deterministic arithmetic, only the empirical interpretation is fenced
